content: How should we handle the case when there is a research solved statement where the answer turned out to be "It's independent of ZFC"? example: FC#4221. I guess our answer(sorry) tag is not so useful in those cases

Moritz Firsching said:

I guess our answer(sorry) tag is not so useful in those cases

I guess someone could just put answer(𝔠 = ℵ_ 1) or something, no?

Can’t we have statements that are independent from ZFC but are mutually exclusive? (I’m concerned that if we used the above, we could end up with false conjectures/theorem statements due to statements that are independent from ZFC but imply/are equivalent to the negation of the continuum hypothesis)
(Of course the negation of the continuum hypothesis is an example of such a statement, but the concern is more that there are (probably?) other such statements that might occur naturally)
E.g this problem is equivalent to the negation of the continuum hypothesis
Could you elaborate a little on what you're worried about with an example?

I guess the point is that while this specific FC#4221 is equivalent to CH there could be some other statement which is not related to CH or any other statement previously known to be independent, but which we can nevertheless prove independent using a tailored argument. (Maybe to clear up confusion, I wasn't trying to suggest that there is some kind of trichotomy where every statement is either true, false or equivalent to CH, sorry if that's how it came across).

If we want to set up a system where people can submit solutions to conjectures and have them assessed automatically, one thing we could build into this system would be the ability to additionally automatically assess claims of the form "I proved this conjecture equivalent to CH", or "I proved this conjecture equivalent to the negation of CH". I think this would be a cool addition, but it would involve hand-coding CH as a statement of specific interest. It would be harder to build a system that allowed people to claim "I proved this statement is independent of ZFC/Lean's type theory" since we would need to model the question in ZFC / embedded Lean type theory.

I think this line of thinking also runs into a philosophical question which has come up in many forms on this Zulip, i.e. "what things are ok to put in an answer() block?"
To answer the original question: I see that the Erdos site has a label for that problem as "independent". Perhaps we could extend our tagging system to include a research independent label.

Better than "independent" would just be to formalize a bunch of mathematical statements known to be independent (such as CH, Martin's axiom MA etc) and then just prove what is actually proved in the paper (e.g. there are combinatorial claims which are known to be true if MA+not(CH) is true, and false if CH is true, and why not just prove this instead rather than saying "independent"). I don't know of any example of a statement which is known to be independent of ZFC without also being known to be related to claims well-known to be independent.

cc @Felix Pernegger
We are trying to solve the same problem at the moment: https://github.com/felixpernegger/pibase-lean/pull/1315

So yeah in https://github.com/felixpernegger/pibase-lean/pull/1315 we have a weak version of independence of ZFC which is exactly what Kevin suggest:
(we need this for general topology where "independent" appears quite a lot)

  1. A curated list of axioms of Type Prop (mathematically) known to be independent, like (G)CH and MA
  2. A list implications between those, like GCH => CH (this list doesnt need to be exhaustive to be useful)
  3. An implementation of "independent" meaning it lies between such a implication (i.e. GCH => P and P => CH)

For the lists in 1. and 2. one has to be careful.

A proper implemenation of "independent" is most likely not possible, so this is the best you can get probably.
Additional annoyances are that GCH requires universe levels and of course Lean's type theory is a bit stronger than normal ZFC.

I'm not personally familiar with this Erdős problem, but I would be interested to hear more about independence from ZFC being difficult to define in Lean. Since projects like flypitch have been successfully completed, is the problem with defining the statement "the interpretation of φ in the language of ZFC is independent of ZFC", as a function of a Prop φ?

Eric Wieser said:

Could you elaborate a little on what you're worried about with an example?

Replying to this a little late, but Bolton's clarification addresses my concern (which was that equivalence to CH is strictly weaker than independence from ZFC since some statements can be also independent from CH, or equivalent to the negation of CH).
I think the proposal of formalising a bunch of propositions that are known to be independent + implications sounds good!

Just a note since Flypitch was mentioned. @Elliot Glazer's recent formalization of Erdos 501 includes a Flypich4 directory that is an port of the original Lean 3 project. I agree that formalizing a number of propositions known to be independent is often the more appropriate solution, but this could be useful occasionally when we really do want independence!
